rubric:
1. Says logistic regression models the probability of a class from labeled examples, rather than an unbounded numeric target the way linear regression does.
2. Defines the logit (log-odds) as a linear score z = w·x + b.
3. Writes the sigmoid 1/(1+e^{−z}) as the map from that score into (0, 1), and notes that a 0.5 threshold is the same cut as z = 0.
4. Says training minimizes binary cross-entropy (logistic loss), −[y ln p + (1−y) ln(1−p)], not squared error on the probability.
5. Says the decision boundary is linear in the features even though the probability is a nonlinear function of z.
